title: Penne con Broccoli
subtitle: Penne with broccoli, garlic, chilli, and anchovy
excerpt: Penne con broccoli is the Italian method for broccoli and pasta: the broccoli is cooked until very soft in the pasta water, then broken down into a rough sauce that coats the penne. Anchovy and garlic give depth; chilli gives heat. The broccoli mainly dissolves into the sauce, giving a result quite different from broccoli tossed raw into pasta.
sourceNotes: Pasta con broccoli is a classic of southern Italian and Sicilian cooking, particularly in Puglia and Campania. The broccoli is typically overcooked by northern European standards: softened to near-mush so it can coat the pasta. The anchovy and garlic base is the standard Puglian treatment.

content.text: In this Italian method, the broccoli cooks until very soft: more than you would for a British side dish: so it can be broken down with a fork or spoon into a coarse sauce. The pasta cooks in the same water, which picks up the broccoli starch. Anchovy is what makes the dish: it dissolves completely in the oil and gives the sauce its savoury depth, with no fishy taste.

items.prepNote: cut into small florets, stalks peeled and sliced

content.text: Bring a large pot of generously salted water to the boil. Add the broccoli and cook for 5 to 6 minutes until very soft, well past the point you would normally stop. Lift out with a slotted spoon, keeping the water boiling.
Add the penne to the broccoli cooking water and cook according to packet instructions, stopping 1 minute short of al dente. Reserve a cup of pasta water before draining.

While the pasta cooks, warm the olive oil in a wide pan over medium heat. Add the garlic and anchovy fillets. Cook for 2 to 3 minutes, pressing the anchovies with a spoon until they dissolve into the oil. Add the chilli flakes.
Add the very soft broccoli to the pan. Break it down with a spoon: not to a smooth paste, but to rough chunks that will cling to the pasta. Add a splash of pasta water to loosen.
Add the drained penne, another splash of pasta water, and toss over medium-high heat for 1 to 2 minutes. The sauce should coat the pasta well. Serve with pecorino if using.

items.symptom: Broccoli stays in hard chunks inside the pasta
items.cause: Broccoli was not cooked long enough before being added to the sauce
items.fix: Cook the broccoli until properly soft: a fork should pass through a floret with very little resistance. The Italian approach requires more cooking time than a British side dish.

items.cause: The anchovies were added to a cold pan and did not dissolve fully into the oil
items.fix: Cook the anchovies in warm oil, pressing and stirring until they melt. Properly dissolved anchovy disappears into the oil and gives depth without fishiness.

items.cause: Not enough pasta water used when tossing
items.fix: Add pasta water gradually while tossing, stopping when the pasta looks glossy and well coated. The starch in the water helps the sauce cling.

content.text: Pasta con broccoli is a standard weeknight dish across southern Italy. In Puglia, orecchiette with broccoli is one of the most well-known pasta pairings in Italian cooking. The anchovy and garlic base is the Puglian version. Some Sicilian versions add pine nuts and raisins. This recipe keeps to the simplest form.
